featureRef: 2.11 Marking a lead as declined, and re-opening it
name: Close an enquiry as not interested, and re-open one closed by mistake
priorityReason: Without it the follow-up list fills with families who already said no, and staff stop trusting it.

goal.capability: to close an enquiry with the reason the family gave, and to re-open one closed by mistake
goal.outcome: the follow-up list holds only live families, and a wrong closure is not a dead end

secondaryActors.involvement: Closes and re-opens enquiries alongside Staff.
Closes and re-opens enquiries, and reviews closures.
Rejects an inquiry at approval, which closes the lead by a different route.
Is the subject of the closure. Is told where the closure follows a rejection.

additional.description: The Principal rejects the inquiry at approval, which closes the lead with the rejection reason.
The Principal rejects the admission after the test, which closes the lead.

preconditions.condition: An enquiry exists and is open — Pending review, Contacted, Visit scheduled or Stale.
For a re-opening, the enquiry is closed as Not interested.

postConditions: The enquiry is on the Not Interested List and no longer appears in the Pending Inquiries List or in any follow-up reminder.
The reason the family gave is recorded and enters loss reporting, which is how the school learns whether it is losing families on fee, distance or timing.
The closure, who did it and when are recorded against the enquiry, and its full contact history stays readable.
A re-opened enquiry is back in the Pending Inquiries List with a fresh follow-up date, and both the closure and the re-opening remain in its history.
Where the closure followed a rejection at approval, the rejection reason is carried onto the closure rather than a second reason being invented.
The enquiry record is not deleted. Nothing about the family is removed.

dataFields.name: Reason
dataFields.validation: Mandatory. A closure with no reason teaches the school nothing (BR-2).
enumValues: No seat in the class wanted

dataFields.name: Other reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters. Required when the reason is Other (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Competitor school
dataFields.validation: Maximum 150 characters. Captured where the family chose another school. Optional, since families often will not say.

dataFields.name: Closing note
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Appended to the contact history, never replacing it.
dataFields.example: Father said they will look again next session.

dataFields.name: Closed by
dataFields.validation: The acting user, or the system where the closure followed a rejection.

dataFields.name: Re-open reason
dataFields.example: Closed in error — the family confirmed they are still interested.

dataFields.name: New follow-up date
dataFields.validation: Not in the past. Set when re-opening so the lead does not disappear again (BR-7).

businessRules.rule: Closing removes the enquiry from the follow-up list and from every reminder. That is the point of it — a list carrying families who already said no stops being trusted.
A reason is mandatory. The purpose of closing is to record why, and a blank reason makes the loss report useless.
Reason Other requires free text. Otherwise Other becomes the default choice and the reason list stops meaning anything.
The enquiry is not deleted. It moves to the Not Interested List and keeps its full contact history, so a family who returns is recognised.
A closed enquiry may be re-opened where it was closed by mistake. Closure is a judgement made in a hurry at a desk, and it has to be reversible.
Re-opening requires a reason, so a lead that is closed and re-opened repeatedly is visible rather than silent.
Re-opening restores the enquiry's previous status and requires a new follow-up date, because an enquiry back in the list with no date disappears again.
The closure and every re-opening stay in the enquiry's history. A re-opened enquiry does not look as though it was never closed.
Where the closure follows a rejection at inquiry approval or at admission approval, the rejection reason is carried onto the closure. A second reason is not invented for the same event.
An enquiry that has been taken forward to a completed admission cannot be closed as not interested. The family is a student.
Closing an enquiry sends nothing to the family by itself. Where the family is to be told, that is a message, sent separately and logged as one.

transitions.condition: The Principal rejects at approval; the rejection reason is carried onto the closure (BR-9).
Re-opened with a reason and a new follow-up date (BR-6, BR-7).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Pending Inquiries → Inquiry detail
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the enquiry with its full contact history.
Opens the reason list, with free text required only for Other.

basicFlow.userAction: Chooses the reason, names the competitor where the family chose another school, and adds any closing note.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Validates that a reason is present, and free text where the reason is Other.
Sets the status to Not interested, records the reason, the person and the date, and appends the closure to the contact log.
Removes the enquiry from the Pending Inquiries List and from every follow-up reminder, and moves it to the Not Interested List.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Not Interested List → Inquiry detail → Re-open
basicFlow.userAction: Re-opens an enquiry closed by mistake, giving a reason and a new follow-up date.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Restores the previous status, returns the enquiry to the Pending Inquiries List, and keeps the closure in its history.

alternateFlows.behaviour: The competitor is captured so the school learns who it is losing families to. It is optional; a refusal to name the school does not block the closure.
alternateFlows.function: closeInquiry(inquiryId, 'Chose another school', null, competitorSchool, note)

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal rejected the inquiry at approval
alternateFlows.navigation: Inquiry decision → Reject → Not Interested List
alternateFlows.behaviour: The enquiry is closed automatically with reason Rejected at approval and the Principal's own reason carried onto the closure. No second reason is invented (BR-9).
alternateFlows.function: closeInquiry(inquiryId, 'Rejected at approval', principalReason, null, null)

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal rejected the admission after the test
alternateFlows.navigation: Applicant decision → Reject → Not Interested List
alternateFlows.behaviour: The same path as A2, with the admission rejection reason carried onto the closure (BR-9).
alternateFlows.function: closeInquiry(inquiryId, 'Rejected at approval', principalReason, null, null)

alternateFlows.condition: A re-opened enquiry is closed again
alternateFlows.behaviour: The second closure is recorded alongside the first. The history shows the family was closed, re-opened and closed again, rather than a single tidy closure (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The family says they may return next session
alternateFlows.behaviour: The intention is recorded in the closing note and stays with the enquiry, so a family who does return is recognised rather than treated as new (BR-4).

openQuestions.question: Is the decline reason list fixed, or should the school be able to add to it?
openQuestions.assumption: Fixed at launch, with Other as the escape.

openQuestions.question: Should a re-opened enquiry return to its previous status or start again at Pending review?
openQuestions.assumption: Its previous status, with a fresh follow-up date (BR-7).

openQuestions.question: Is there a limit on how many times a lead may be closed and re-opened?
openQuestions.assumption: No limit; every event is recorded.

openQuestions.question: Should the family be told automatically when their enquiry is closed?
openQuestions.assumption: No. Closing sends nothing; a message is sent separately where the school wants to (BR-11).

openQuestions.question: May a closed enquiry still be re-opened after the 3-year retention has passed?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
